title: Beyond the LLM: BLLM and the Entropy Law of Sound Recursive Self-Improvement: paper, Lean 4 formalization and verification code
description:
A BLLM is a language model that keeps a modification of itself only after a randomized check of soundness epsilon accepts it. We prove that the least cost of certifying modifications of total cost A with at most theta expected false acceptances is (A/log(1/epsilon))(H(p) + log(1/theta)) up to an additive A, where H(p) is the entropy of the cost profile; Huffman codes give the exact optimum, Renyi entropies govern checks of polynomial order, a duality criterion decides which infinite cost sequences admit sound schedules, checking every step of a chain is exponentially cheaper than checking its outcome, an infinite self-improvement of finite cost can be sound exactly when the sum of a_n log(1/a_n) converges, and a branching takeoff needs check strength growing linearly in the generation. The results hold in a model with independent runs, perfect completeness and schedules fixed in advance.

preprintBeyondTheLLM/ holds the paper as a PDF; BLLM/paper/ holds the REVTeX source with its figures; dist/ holds the PDF, the LaTeX source zip and the arXiv tarball. BLLM/lean/ is a Lean 4 and Mathlib project with thirty-nine theorems, each depending only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. BLLM/checks/ contains independent checks in Python, C and C++ (33,505 checks); BLLM/checks/run_all.sh runs them and builds the Lean project. The probabilistic limit theorems are proved or cited in the paper and are not formalized.
